submission.justification: Simulated time resolution (100k events each): G2 is best at every gap (0.875 ns at 2 mm, 1.07 ns at 1 mm, 1.01 ns at 3 mm), then G1 (1.31 ns at 2 mm), then G3 (2.02 ns at 2 mm; 2.19 ns at 1 mm; 2.41 ns at 3 mm). Within each mixture, 2 mm is the best gap for G1, G2 and G3 among the tested points. However, no project document gives GWP100 values for any candidate, so the hard GWP <= 150 requirement cannot be verified for any mixture. G2 is described as the standard fluorinated mixture, which typically has a high GWP, so it is likely non-compliant and I did not recommend it. G1 is only a partial substitute for the fluorinated component and is also likely above the limit. G3 is based on newer replacement gases and is the most plausible candidate to meet the limit, at the cost of roughly 2.3x worse time resolution than G2. I recommend G3 at 2 mm only as a provisional choice. Its GWP100 must be confirmed from supplier data before the choice is final. If G3 fails the limit, the next option is G1 at 2 mm, which would also need its GWP checked.

requirements.requirement: Mixture must be one of the three candidates in candidate_specs.md
requirements.evidence: Mixture-G3 is one of the listed candidates.

No project document gives GWP100 values for G1, G2 or G3. G3 is chosen as the most plausible candidate because it is based on newer replacement gases, but this is not verified. Supplier GWP data must be checked before the choice is final.
G3 at 2 mm gives 2.021 ns, worse than G2 (0.875 ns at 2 mm) and G1 (1.308 ns at 2 mm). The G3 choice trades time resolution for the likely GWP compliance.
